activity_records.description: Wire 5.3: activity record values, built from messages.json's messages, and the record keys they sit at under the fixed policy, blinded with their reader's naming key: alice's for payer_activity, bob's for payee_activity. Some members only some records carry: request_hash and billing_period only a period record, attempt_id and unrequested only the record of a payment without a request, and allowance_id only a payer's request record. accepted are records their reader binds at their keys; refused are the same records with a member where their binding and side don't allow it, which their reader refuses, and, last, alice's request records storing a request whose sender's certificate doesn't allow it (wire 5.2, the sender's side of check 8): messages.json label_rejections' request labelled shop2 from bob's hosted app, which holds only request:shop1, and messages.json's payment_request presented with documents.json's chat-only certificate of the shop's keys, at the keys their requests name. Appended after them, on payment evidence (wire 4.11): accepted, records whose receipt is of the stored proof's attempt, or of the record's attempt_id; refused, the same with a receipt of another attempt. reason is paykit-lib's wording, of the first check that refuses it.

allowance_records.description: Wire 4.16, 5.4: allowances record values of alice's, built from binding_accepted's record and messages.json's Allowance messages, some signed again by their sender with refs or sides changed, at the record key binding_accepted gives. A response refers to the proposal; an end refers to the proposal and the stored acceptance; an end referring to the proposal alone is its sender's withdrawal, before any response; a rejected Allowance has no end; executor_app_id comes only in an acceptance, from the allower. accepted are records a reader binds; refused are those it refuses, the last a record whose rejection carries executor_app_id, which check 10 drops. reason is paykit-lib's wording.

description: Paykit's sealed record values (wire 5), sealed as the Switch's sealed values are (the Switch set's sealed.json) under alice's scope_key(2, "pay") from the Switch set's keys.json, with record keys blinded with alice's naming key. binding_accepted holds record values, as they are sealed, that a reader binds to their record keys, recomputed with alice's naming key (wire 5.4, 5.5): a payment_lists record, an allowances record and its allowance_ledgers record, checked against that allowances record. binding_rejections holds the same values at a wrong key or with a field that doesn't match, a list record whose payee isn't the identity that sent its list (bob's list, filed under payee alice at the key of alice and the shop's App ID) and an acceptance naming another Allowance, each of which a reader refuses. labelled is a payee record of a labelled request. activity_records holds activity records a reader binds, and the same records with a member their binding and side don't allow, which it refuses. allowance_records holds allowances records a reader binds or refuses by their messages' lifecycle.

labelled.description: Wire 5.1, 5.3: bob's payee_activity record of messages.json's payment_request_labelled, holding the request and alice's acceptance, under the labelled policy read_scope request:shop1, write_scopes [request:shop1], at the record key that policy's hash gives (identifiers.json), sealed with bob's label key for shop1 at data epoch 1 (keys.json sub_scope_keys) and AAD lp("pubky-switch/v1/sealed", identity, "request:shop1", record key). The request key and another label's key don't open it. rejections are records a reader refuses: a labelled policy must name the label of the request the record holds, and the fixed policy an unlabelled request; reason is the prototype's wording.

msg_ids_bounds.description: Wire 5.3, 5.4: binding_accepted's payment_lists record with msg_ids replaced, and the msg_ids its reader keeps (kept), which a writer writes: the ID of each message the record stores, then the 16 newest distinct IDs of the others it names, oldest first, each once.
